source_text: Qui autem in Christo hoc est in lumine semper sumus nec noctibus ab oratione cessemus. sic Anna uidua sine intermissione rogans semper et uigilans perseuerabat in promerendo Deo, sicut in euangelio scriptum est: non recedebat de templo ieiuniis et orationibus seruiens nocte et die. uiderint uel gentiles qui necdum inluminati sunt uel Iudaei qui deserti lumine in tenebris remanserunt : nos, fratres dilectissimi, qui in Domini luce semper sumus, qui meminimus et tenemus quid esse accepta gratia coeperimus, conputemus noctem pro die. ambulare nos credamus semper in lumine, non impediamur a tenebris quas euasimus, nulla sint horis nocturnis precum damna, nulla orationum pigra et ignaua dispendia. per Dei indulgentiam recreati spiritaliter et renati imitemur quod futuri sumus: habituri in regno sine interuentu noctis solum diem sic nocte quasi in luce uigilemus, oraturi semper et acturi gratias Deo hic quoque orare et gratias agere non desinamus.
thought_title: Night as day for those in Christ
orientation: Cyprian is closing the treatise by urging Christians, who live in Christ the true light, to keep praying even at night.
pass_a_gloss: Who [are] however in Christ this is in [the] light always we are nor [by] nights from prayer may we cease. so Anna [the] widow without intermission asking always and watching she persevered in meriting God, just as in the gospel [it] is written: not she departed from the temple [with] fastings and prayers serving night and day. let [them] have seen either [the] gentiles who not yet enlightened are or [the] Jews who deserted [by the] light in darkness have remained : we, brothers most beloved, who in [the] Lord's light always are, who we remember and hold what [we] having received grace have begun to be, let us count [the] night for [the] day. [to] walk us let us believe always in [the] light, not let us be hindered by [the] darkness which we have escaped, none let there be [in] hours nightly of prayers losses, none of prayers lazy and idle waste. through God's indulgence recreated spiritually and reborn let us imitate what [we] are about to be: [about] to have in [the] kingdom without [the] intervention of night only [the] day so [by] night as in [the] light let us watch, [about] to pray always and [about] to give thanks [to] God here also to pray and thanks to give not let us cease.

choices.english: let the gentiles see to it
choices.why: The verb is a third-person plural perfect subjunctive used as a dismissive imperative; 'see to it' preserves the distancing force without adding a modern idiom.
The passive participle with ablative of agent keeps the sense that the light has abandoned them, matching Cyprian's contrast with those who are in the light.

choices.english: let us count night as day
choices.why: The verb 'conputemus' is a hortatory subjunctive; 'count' preserves the reckoning metaphor and the hortatory force.
rejected: let us reckon night for day
let us consider night as day

choices.term: nulla sint horis nocturnis precum damna
choices.english: let there be no losses of prayers in the night hours
choices.why: The jussive subjunctive 'sint' is rendered with 'let there be' to keep the command-like wish; 'losses' preserves the commercial metaphor of 'damna'.
rejected: let no losses of prayers be

choices.why: 'Dispendia' means wasteful expenditure or loss; 'wastings' keeps the economic metaphor and the negative moral coloring of 'pigra et ignaua'.

choices.term: per Dei indulgentiam recreati spiritaliter et renati
choices.english: recreated spiritually and reborn through the indulgence of God
choices.why: The passive participles are causal; 'indulgentiam' is rendered 'indulgence' to preserve the theological term for God's gracious pardon, and 'recreated' keeps the prefix 're-' of 'recreati'.
rejected: refreshed spiritually and reborn by God's indulgence
renewed spiritually and reborn through God's kindness

bible_refs.note: non recedebat de templo ieiuniis et orationibus seruiens nocte et die

pass_b_english: But we who are in Christ—that is, in the light—are always in the light, and we must not cease from prayer even in the nights. So Anna the widow, praying without interruption, always watchful, persisted in deserving well of God, as it is written in the Gospel: "She did not withdraw from the temple, serving with fastings and prayers night and day" (Luke 2:37). Let the gentiles see to it—those not yet enlightened—or the Jews, who have been forsaken by the light and have remained in darkness. But we, dearly beloved brothers, who are always in the light of the Lord, who remember and hold what we have begun to be through the grace we have received, let us count night as day. Let us believe that we are always walking in the light; let us not be hindered by the darkness we have escaped. Let there be no losses of prayers in the night hours, no lazy and slothful wastings of prayer. Recreated spiritually and reborn through the indulgence of God, let us imitate what we shall be: we who will possess in the kingdom only day, without the interruption of night, let us keep watch in the night as in the light. We who will always pray and give thanks to God, let us not cease to pray and give thanks here as well.

last_rejected.quote: Let the gentiles see to it
last_rejected.why: "Uiderint" is jussive/subjunctive "let them see to it/let them look after themselves," but "uel" means "or"—the Latin says "let the gentiles OR the Jews see to it," not addressing gentiles as a command. The English "Let the gentiles see to it" misreads "uel" as vocative or appositive, changing the syntax and force.
last_rejected.fix: Let the gentiles or the Jews see to it—those not yet enlightened, or those forsaken by the light.
last_rejected.ruling: English 'Let the gentiles see to it—or the Jews' preserves 'uiderint uel gentiles...uel Iudaei'; 'uel' as 'or' is intact.

last_rejected.quote: persisted in deserving well of God
last_rejected.why: "Promerendo Deo" means "in winning God's favor/merit," not "deserving well of God" which suggests Anna deserved well herself. The Latin has God as object of the service, not Anna as deserving subject.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Deserving well of God' is a normal rendering of 'promerendo Deo'; no meaning is changed or lost.

last_rejected.why: The Latin uses subjunctive "cessemus" in a purpose/result clause with "qui...sumus" (we who are...let us not cease), not indicative "must not." The English "must not" imposes obligation where Latin has hortatory subjunctive.
last_rejected.fix: let us not cease from prayer even in the nights
last_rejected.ruling: 'Must not cease' adequately renders hortatory subjunctive 'cessemus'; obligation is the normal force.

last_rejected.quote: We who will always pray and give thanks to God
last_rejected.source_quote: oraturi semper et acturi gratias Deo
last_rejected.why: The English omits "acturi gratias" structure—"we who will always pray and give thanks" merges two future participles but loses the parallel "oraturi...acturi" (about to pray...about to give thanks). More critically, "hic quoque" (here also) is rendered as "here as well" but the participial construction "oraturi...acturi" is flattened.
last_rejected.fix: We who are about to pray always and give thanks to God, let us not cease to pray and give thanks here as well
last_rejected.ruling: 'Will always pray and give thanks' preserves both 'oraturi' and 'acturi gratias'; 'hic quoque' rendered as 'here as well'.
